courses.title: Project Management Fundamentals
courses.summary: Plan, run and close projects on time and on budget using proven tools and templates.
courses.description:
By the end of this course you will be able to:

- Define a project's scope, objectives and stakeholders
- Build a work breakdown structure and a realistic schedule
- Track progress, risks and budget
- Report status clearly to managers and clients

Includes downloadable templates, a final exam and a certificate of completion.

lessons.title: What makes a project a project
lessons.body:
## Projects vs. operations

A **project** is temporary and creates something unique. **Operations** are ongoing and repetitive.

| | Project | Operations |
|---|---|---|
| Duration | Has a start and end | Continuous |
| Output | Unique result | Repeated output |
| Example | Opening a new branch | Running the branch |

> **Tip:** If you can't say when it ends, it is probably not a project yet.

lessons.title: Scope and the work breakdown structure
lessons.body:
Watch the walkthrough, then practise on your own project.

### Steps
1. Write the project objective in one sentence.
2. List the major deliverables.
3. Break each deliverable into work packages small enough to estimate (8-80 hours).

lessons.title: Scheduling with milestones
lessons.body:
## Milestones

A milestone marks a significant point - it has **no duration**.

- Sign-off of requirements
- Prototype approved
- Go-live

### Critical path
The longest chain of dependent tasks. Any delay on it delays the whole project.

lessons.title: Managing risks
lessons.body:
## Risk register

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| Key supplier late | Medium | High | Second supplier on standby |
| Budget cut | Low | High | Prioritised scope list |

Review the register at every status meeting.

lessons.title: Essential formulas: SUM, AVERAGE, IF
lessons.body:
## Three formulas to start with

- `=SUM(B2:B20)` adds a range
- `=AVERAGE(B2:B20)` gives the mean
- `=IF(C2>=50,"Pass","Fail")` returns one of two values

Practise with the attached workbook.
